skill.name: reviewdog
skill.description: Configure reviewdog to collect security scanner and linter results in CI, then publish focused pull request feedback.
skill.summary: Adds reviewdog guidance for security scanner feedback in pull requests and merge requests.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: The skill is primarily documentation and CI templates for reviewdog-based security scanning. Most static findings are expected scanner commands, CI token references, or security reference examples. The GitLab CI template contains a confirmed pipe-to-shell remote installer, and fixed /tmp Gitleaks paths should be replaced.

remediation.issue: GitLab CI template pipes a remote installer script directly into sh.
remediation.suggestion: Install reviewdog from a pinned release, package manager, or verified binary with checksum validation before execution.

remediation.issue: Gitleaks examples use a predictable /tmp/gitleaks.json path.
remediation.suggestion: Use mktemp or a CI workspace-scoped filename, then remove the report after reviewdog consumes it.

remediation.issue: CI examples rely on repository tokens for posting review comments.
remediation.suggestion: Document minimum token permissions and prefer platform-scoped tokens with pull request comment access only.

remediation.issue: Several examples use floating latest or main references for tools and containers.
remediation.suggestion: Pin action versions, container tags, scanner versions, and ruleset versions for reproducible security reviews.

content.value_statement: Security findings often arrive too late or outside code review. This skill helps configure reviewdog to post scanner results where developers already work.
actual_capabilities: Explains reviewdog setup for GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, and local pre-commit workflows.
Shows how to route Bandit, Semgrep, Gitleaks, Hadolint, Checkov, and ShellCheck output into reviewdog.
Provides sample reviewdog configuration for severity levels, fail behavior, and diff filtering.
Maps common scanner findings to CWE and OWASP categories for clearer review comments.
Documents reporter formats for GitHub, GitLab, Gerrit, local output, and custom rdjson input.
limitations: It provides templates and guidance, not a managed scanner service.
Teams must install and pin reviewdog and each scanner in their own CI environment.
Scanner accuracy depends on the selected tools, rulesets, and repository language coverage.
The documentation mentions bundled scripts, but this snapshot only includes templates and references.

use_cases.title: Add PR Security Comments
use_cases.description: Configure reviewdog so SAST and secret findings appear as inline pull request comments.

use_cases.title: Standardize CI Scanner Output
use_cases.description: Unify multiple scanner formats into reviewdog reporters for GitHub Actions or GitLab CI.

use_cases.title: Shift Findings Left
use_cases.description: Use pre-commit and diff-aware reviewdog settings to flag new issues before merge.

prompt_templates.prompt: Review my reviewdog setup and suggest filter modes, severity levels, and fail rules that reduce false positives.

prompt_templates.prompt: Create a reviewdog plan for Semgrep, Bandit, Gitleaks, Hadolint, and Checkov across GitHub Actions.

output_examples.input: A team wants Bandit findings to appear only on new Python lines in pull requests.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends a GitHub Actions reviewdog workflow with added-line filtering, pull request review reporting, and blocking on error severity.

output_examples.input: A platform team has Semgrep, Checkov, and Gitleaks results in separate CI logs.
output: The skill outlines a shared reviewdog workflow for each tool.
It recommends severity thresholds and reporter choices for merge request discussions.
It notes where token permissions and scanner version pinning should be configured.

output_examples.input: A security engineer needs guidance for a custom scanner format.
output_examples.output: The skill points to reviewdog diagnostic format concepts and suggests mapping messages, locations, severity, and CWE links.

best_practices: Pin reviewdog, scanner, action, and container versions before using the templates in production.
Use least-privilege CI tokens and store them only in the platform secret manager.
Start with diff-aware filtering, then widen coverage after teams agree on severity thresholds.
anti_patterns: Do not pipe remote installer scripts directly into a shell in trusted CI jobs.
Do not give reviewdog broad repository tokens when pull request comment permissions are enough.
Do not fail every build on untriaged low-severity findings from newly enabled scanners.

faq.question: Does this skill run scanners by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides reviewdog configuration guidance and templates that you adapt to your CI environment.

faq.question: Which tools does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers reviewdog integrations for Semgrep, Bandit, Gitleaks, Hadolint, Checkov, ShellCheck, and custom formats.

faq.question: Can it work with GitHub and GitLab?
faq.answer: Yes. The included guidance covers GitHub pull request reviews and GitLab merge request discussions.

faq.question: Does it replace a security scanner?
faq.answer: No. Reviewdog publishes scanner results. You still choose, install, and maintain the underlying scanners.

faq.question: How should teams manage tokens?
faq.answer: Use platform secrets, minimum permissions, branch protections, and regular rotation for every CI token.

faq.question: Is the included GitLab installer safe as written?
faq.answer: No. Replace remote pipe-to-shell installation with a pinned release, checksum verification, or trusted package source.
